title: Soft Turn
oneSentenceMeaning: A spoken thought opens into a page you can keep shaping, with one broad fold joining the two.
appIdentity: Mluva makes speaking feel like a natural way to begin useful written work. On an Omarchy desktop, a shortcut opens a small moment of capture; that speech becomes editable text, and an optional rewrite can help give it structure. Its identity should carry the ease of that transition and the confidence of being able to return to the original recognition. The app supports local and cloud choices independently for speech and rewriting, so the brand expresses user agency without implying that every operation stays on the device. Markdown, saved versions and retained source make the result feel like material the user owns and can continue working with. The tone is calm, direct and quietly pleasurable. “Most delightful dictation for Omarchy” is the product promise; “A little more delight every day” describes the cumulative feeling. The mark should belong beside practical desktop tools while suggesting a gentler entry into writing.
markIdentity: Soft Turn gives the existing idea of an unfolding thought a more readable destination: a page. One compact filled shape contains a broad upper fold, an upright lower plane and a short speech-like extension at the lower left. A generous diagonal opening enters from the right, making the turn visible through genuine negative space. The two areas remain connected by a substantial left hinge. This is a graphic gesture of speech settling into something editable, rather than a diagram of the application's stages. The retained connection can support the story of keeping the original alongside revisions, but the logo does not claim to communicate that feature without explanation. Its upper portion feels open and conversational; its lower portion feels settled and usable. The balance between soft outer corners and one deliberate angular opening makes it both approachable and precise. It remains an abstract app emblem at a glance, with a speech-to-page reading available on a second look.
logoDescription:
Build a compact, nearly square emblem from a single contiguous filled silhouette. Its footprint should feel more like a thick sheet caught in one modest turn than a document icon. The top is somewhat narrower than the lower portion. A broad, softly squared upper shoulder runs toward the right and then descends to the outer tip of the fold. Below it, a more upright lower plane supplies a calm right edge and an almost level base. The left side joins these regions in one continuous, substantial mass. Keep the overall stance upright; the interior diagonal supplies enough movement without rotating the whole mark.

The defining feature is a wide open notch entering from the right at approximately the upper two-fifths of the height. It travels diagonally down and left at roughly twenty-five degrees, ending just left of the optical center. Give this inner end a short, blunt return rather than a needle point. The notch separates two broad areas of the same opaque ink and opens directly into the transparent background. Its shape implies one turning layer without using a drawn crease, a second color or a shadow. The upper area should remain a substantial flap, not a thin ribbon. The lower area should occupy slightly more visual mass so the emblem settles rather than flies.

At the lower left, allow the base to resolve into a short, blunt, down-left extension. This is the only speech cue. It should emerge naturally from the contour and project less than one-tenth of the total height. Avoid a long chat-bubble pointer: the mark must stay compact, and the page-like plane should remain the principal reading. Use modest corner softening on exposed shoulders and the lower right, while preserving the diagonal opening as a clearly intentional cut.

Render the shape in one fully opaque ink on actual transparent alpha. There is no enclosing tile, outline, ruled text, paper texture, folded dog-ear, perspective shading or decorative perforation. At twenty-four pixels, the notch must read as a deliberate opening and the left hinge as solid material. At large size, the same silhouette should reward inspection through proportion and optical balance. The intended result is a quiet, tactile emblem whose meaning comes from one clear physical gesture: a thought turning into a usable page.
wordmarkDescription:
Set the exact name “Mluva”, with an uppercase M and lowercase luva. Begin with JetBrains Mono Medium outlines so the lettering belongs naturally to the application and film typography. Preserve the font's readable construction and practical character, then make a compact bespoke word rather than retaining equal character cells. The wordmark should feel composed and steady beside the folded symbol. It should not imitate paper folding across every letter or ask the reader to decode an experimental alphabet.

Keep the M upright and generous enough to establish the name immediately. Its interior diagonals should remain open at small sizes; soften their optical joins only enough to prevent dark clots. Narrow the l visibly, retaining a short entry flag and a modest right-facing foot so it cannot become an uppercase I. The foot may finish in a shallow chamfer related to the mark's twenty-five-degree opening. This is a quiet detail for larger artwork, not a feature on which recognition depends. Keep the u's bowl open and its right stem unambiguous. Give the v a clean inner valley and slightly blunt its lowest point to balance the softened symbol. Preserve a clearly double-storey a; open its counter and avoid a terminal that looks like a second fold or arrow.

Use optical spacing rather than a tracking value applied to all pairs. Close the M–l gap enough that the narrow l belongs to the word, let l–u breathe around the l foot, and slightly tighten the diagonal white space between u–v and v–a. These are starting directions for outline review, not approved numeric kerns. Maintain an even baseline and a comfortable lowercase height, around three-quarters of the M cap height. The word should read as one rhythm, with no exaggerated gap after the first letter.

Match the emblem through substantial ink, restrained corner softening and one consistent diagonal detail. Export the wordmark alone in the same solid monochrome on transparent alpha. Preserve font provenance when real outlines are produced. No symbol, tagline, border, underline, alternate spelling or background belongs in this asset. Final acceptance requires an exact five-letter read and a visual check of the narrowed l.

selfCritique.concern: The fold could read as a generic document or notes app before it reads as speech.
selfCritique.response: The short lower-left extension supplies a restrained conversational cue, while the right-hand opening replaces the conventional dog-ear. The product descriptor will still carry category clarity; the mark alone should not be expected to explain dictation.

selfCritique.concern: A long diagonal and pointed flap could resemble a paper airplane, send icon or familiar messaging mark.
selfCritique.response: Keep the stance upright, the lower plane heavier, the upper tip blunt and the speech extension short. Reject any render whose dominant gesture aims forward or whose upper flap becomes a narrow triangular wing.

selfCritique.concern: The meaning is still partially interpretive.
selfCritique.response: The page destination and visible turn are more concrete than a free abstract loop, but this concept needs a quick unprompted recognition comparison against the other territories. No distinctiveness or recognition claim has been tested.

selfCritique.concern: The notch could disappear or merge into a hairline at panel size.
selfCritique.response: The revision widens it to roughly three pixels at a twenty-four-pixel silhouette height, with a blunt inner return and a broad connecting hinge. Inspect an actual raster before accepting those dimensions.

selfCritique.concern: JetBrains Mono could make the result feel like plain product text, while too much customization would weaken its useful familiarity.
selfCritique.response: Concentrate changes in the l width, pair spacing, counter balance and a single subtle terminal chamfer. Keep the M, u, v and double-storey a plainly recognizable.

revision.name: Widen the turn; settle the page
revision.initialIdea: The first construction used a long pointed upper flap, a narrow diagonal crease and a triangular speech tail. Its meaning depended on a delicate paper-fold detail, while the combined points gave it too much forward motion.
revision.critique: At the specification stage, the narrow crease looked likely to collapse at twenty-four pixels, and the pointed construction risked becoming an airplane or send icon. The tail also added a second competing diagonal.
changes: Replace the crease with an open transparent notch approximately twelve to fourteen percent of total silhouette height at its narrow practical section.
End the notch with a short blunt return and retain a connecting left hinge at least twenty-four percent of silhouette width.
Shorten the upper flap and increase the lower plane's visual mass so the mark stays upright and settled.
Reduce the speech extension to a short blunt projection below ten percent of total height.
Keep the wordmark's fold reference to one shallow l-foot chamfer; remove proposed cuts from the other letters.
revision.result: The revised specification has one dominant turn, a more durable negative space and a quieter page-like posture. The logo and wordmark descriptions and prompts below describe this revised version.
revision.verificationStatus: Design-specification revision only. No image, vector proof, small-size raster or similarity review has been produced by this concept agent.

logoPrompt: Create ONE standalone modern app logo symbol for Mluva, with no lettering anywhere. Concept: Soft Turn, a spoken thought opening into an editable page. Make a compact upright near-square SINGLE CONTIGUOUS SOLID SILHOUETTE, filled in fully opaque near-black ink. One broad upper folded flap and a heavier upright lower page-like plane remain fused through a thick left hinge. The top is a little narrower than the bottom. A GENEROUS OPEN DIAGONAL NOTCH enters from the right at about two-fifths of the height and travels down-left around twenty-five degrees, ending just left of center in a blunt return; this notch is transparent empty space, not a stroke, and is thick enough to remain clearly open at a twenty-four-pixel symbol height, about three pixels equivalent. The upper flap is broad and blunt, never a pointed wing. The lower plane has a calm near-vertical right edge, a mostly level base, subtly softened outer corners, and one very short blunt down-left extension emerging from its lower-left contour as a gentle speech cue. Keep the left hinge substantial. The whole mark feels like one thick sheet making one quiet turn, with real page-like mass, not an origami illustration. Use a perfectly flat single color with crisp vector-like edges and only normal edge antialiasing. Output a genuinely TRANSPARENT RGBA PNG background, including through the diagonal opening, with comfortable clear space around the centered emblem. No enclosing square or app tile, no outline or strokes, no microphone, no soundwave, no leaf, no paper airplane, no triangular send icon, no folded document dog-ear, no text lines, no gradient, no shading, no shadow, no glow, no texture, no checkerboard image, no background plate, no caption, no mockup, no variant sheet. One symbol only.
wordmarkPrompt: Create ONE standalone wordmark reading EXACTLY Mluva, five letters, uppercase M and lowercase luva, with NO icon. Start from the forms of JetBrains Mono Medium and make restrained optical refinements: a confidently upright M with open interior diagonals; a visibly narrowed lowercase l that retains a short entry flag and a modest right-facing foot; clear u; clean v with a very slightly blunted bottom; unmistakable double-storey a with an open counter. Use substantial, even ink weight and tiny optical softening at joins, never rounded bubble lettering. The l foot alone may have a shallow twenty-five-degree end chamfer, a subtle reference to a folded page; do not cut or split other letters. Keep a stable baseline and lowercase height about three-quarters of the M height. Space the word optically as a cohesive compact name, avoiding monospaced character cells and avoiding a gap after M: M–l close but readable, l–u balanced around the foot, u–v and v–a gently tightened. Render the full word as solid fully opaque near-black filled letterforms with crisp vector-like edges. Output a genuinely TRANSPARENT RGBA PNG, wide composition with comfortable clear space, the word centered and completely visible. No symbol, no extra letters or words, no tagline, no caption, no underline, no outline strokes, no stencil gaps, no ligature that obscures letters, no color variation, no gradient, no lighting, no shadow, no texture, no glow, no enclosing tile, no checkerboard image, no mockup, no background. One exact Mluva wordmark only.
smallSizeRisks: At twenty-four pixels of silhouette height, the notch should retain roughly three pixels of open width through its important section; inspect both black-on-light and white-on-dark rasterizations.
The notch's blunt inner end can become a dark clog under downsampling; adjust the inner return before increasing the entire icon's weight.
The short speech extension may lose its meaning below twenty-four pixels. The folded page silhouette must remain useful without that cue; do not enlarge the tail into a competing arrow.
A thin upper flap would turn into a ribbon or detached shard. Keep its practical thickness comparable to the lower plane's strongest areas.
At small wordmark heights the l-foot chamfer may vanish. Exact reading and even spacing take priority, and the l must remain distinct from I or an accidental gap.
Transparent alpha and silhouette clarity remain unverified until the parent produces and inspects actual assets.
opticalRules: Use one opaque fill and genuine transparent negative space; do not simulate depth with gray planes, shadows or outlines.
Keep the silhouette approximately as wide as it is tall, upright, with the lower plane carrying slightly more visual weight.
Use a diagonal opening around twenty-five degrees from horizontal, entering from the right and terminating just left of optical center.
Target twelve to fourteen percent of total silhouette height for the useful notch width, then refine against an actual twenty-four-pixel raster.
Retain a left hinge no narrower than roughly one-quarter of total silhouette width; the mark must read as one connected object.
Blunt the fold tip and speech extension; the extension projects less than ten percent of total height.
Use only modest corner radii, around four to six percent of silhouette height on the outer shoulders; avoid an enclosing rounded-square contour.
Balance by visible mass rather than bounding-box center; the lower-left extension must not drag the apparent mark left.
For the exact Mluva wordmark, use JetBrains Mono Medium as provenance, preserve a double-storey a and a recognizable flagged l, and adjust pair spacing optically.
In a future lockup, begin with symbol height around one-and-a-quarter times the M cap height and a gap around half the cap height; confirm balance only after real outlines exist.
Provide at least one-quarter of symbol height as clear space, and keep the wordmark independent for tiny launcher or panel uses.
motionRelationship: A future reveal can open the existing diagonal notch by a small amount while the lower plane and left hinge stay anchored, then settle into the final static silhouette. The movement should be one soft turn, not a sequence of origami folds or an endless paper flutter. Keep it brief and use a calm ease without spring overshoot; do not imply a measured transcription speed. The wordmark can appear as one stable word once the mark has nearly settled, with no letter-by-letter scrambling. In the film, the emblem can sit quietly over the supplied water footage while the real background supplies the fluidity. It may share the application's gentle 3.4-second cadence only as a very small optional breathing variation, without closing the notch or changing recognition. Reduced motion uses the final still mark immediately. The chosen logo should remain fully meaningful with motion disabled.
